newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch forwarders set acceptance fee deadlines.
newsitem.headline: Dutch forwarders set acceptance fee deadlines.

text.p: Dutch forwarders have set staged deadlines after which they will no longer pay a controversial "acceptance fee" that handling companies charge forwarders.

NVVL, the Dutch freight forwarders association, have given an ultimatum in their determination to put an end to the fee. Forwarders will only pay half of the fees in 1997 and from 1998 they will no longer pay the fees, said Hans Knuvers, spokesman for the NVVL.
The fee, usually around 15 guilders, is added to most consignments and has been in dispute for at least four years.

Handling companies argue that they have to carry out certain activities when they accept consignments, such as registration and administration work. And sometimes cargo is not properly ready for carriage, a spokesman for the NVLA, the handlers association, said.
The fee has traditionally boosted the handling companies profits by eight million guilders a year, industry sources estimated.
A mediator was brought in at the end of last year and a report has been carried out into thedispute.
Forwarders are following the recommendations of the report in aiming to phase the fee out, but handling companies have yet to agree.
The NVLA spokesman said the handling companies want compensation, they are doing a job and should be paid. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
